### K5 red team · Question

Event: `04b6db60e985acefbe9addd2bf4da1ea` · 2026-09-24T21:07:29Z

> K5b plan v1 red-team review (answer 173, Q147, D3-plan-review R1). Read against the orchestrator's OD1-OD7 rulings, KERNEL-SPEC R3/R10/I5, and the kernel at wp-k5 ce95d19ba: legacy MapMemory, map_range, ownership paths, grants.rs.
> 
> VERDICT: BLOCK on P1-1 (one rule to make explicit, plus a test). Otherwise sound: OD1 (release-time trigger) and the DMA_OWNER sentinel are the right design, and they close the generic free, move and lend paths by construction. P2s to fold into v2.
> 
> Verified by code reading:
> - Only dma_alloc discloses a physical address. The legacy VirtToPhys call is not served (UnhandledSyscall), and legacy MapMemory refuses any range that touches RAM (syscall.rs ~880).
> - Every generic release, move and lend path checks the caller's ownership (release_page, claim_release_move, free_frame_of, move_frame). With the frames owned by DMA_OWNER, none of them can free a DMA frame, including legacy Move/Lend messages and legacy UnmapMemory.
> - process_map moves only is_main_memory pages of the caller's own, so MMIO can't be passed down.
> - A process_create rollback child never ran, so it holds no runs.
> - dma_release inside terminate is non-preemptible, and reset-then-pool happens in one critical section, so no device can be re-armed in between.
> - The window is safe from user space: U bit clear, legacy MapMemory is refused at or above USER_AREA_END for pid != 1, and map_fixed is limited to user space.
> 
> P1-1 A device that is already quarantined must count as NOT reset for every later release.
> s2 step 2 says 'reset every slot in S that is not already quarantined', and step 3 pools runs 'if every reset in S confirmed'. Under the natural reading, a skipped quarantined slot passes step 3.
> Scenario: P1 and P2 both hold runs allocated through device A. P1 dies; A fails its reset, so P1's runs are quarantined and A is flagged. P2 lives on, and A, never successfully reset, still holds ring addresses. P2 dies: A is in S but skipped. If that counts as confirmed, P2's runs go to the pool, which is exactly Q147's arbitrary-DMA hazard.
> The epoch assert doesn't catch it: any successful reset of A after P2's alloc (say a third holder's death, before A broke) satisfies reset_epoch > run.epoch.
> Fix:
> (a) State the rule: a quarantined slot in S means every run of the dying pid is quarantined. Alternatively, quarantine every live run on A at flag time, pooling none later.
> (b) Make the assert specific to this release: record the epoch each slot reached in this dma_release and require it for every run's slot.
> (c) Add a model mutation (e.g. K5bQuarantinedSlotCountsAsReset) and a boot sub-case in dma-reset-quarantine: a second holder on the deaf device dies after the first, and its frames never return.
> 
> P2-1 Legacy MMIO mappings bypass both the reset set and the quarantine flag.
> A grant-holding legacy process can MapMemory a virtio device's MMIO (grants::may_map_device) with no handle. Two consequences:
> (1) It can allocate through device A's handle and drive device B through its legacy mapping. B is not in S, so B keeps the freed frames' addresses.
> (2) A quarantined device stays reachable this way.
> interrupt_claim already refuses IRQs that have a device object ('a source with a device object is R5's'). Do the same for MMIO: refuse legacy MapMemory of any range owned by a device object or registry slot. Otherwise add legacy-mapped registry devices to the process's S bitmask and flag check. Test it in dma-rules.
> 
> P2-2 OD5's over-limit force-charge breaks I5 (usage <= limit). The R3 it cites doesn't allow over-limit: a lend is charged when the receiver takes it, within that receiver's limit.
> A simpler rule keeps I5: quarantine keeps the charge where it already is (the run's charged budget, already paid within its limit). destroy_marked moves it to the destroyed top's parent before return_carve. That parent then gets back the child's carve (>= its usage >= the quarantined pages), so it never goes over its limit, and free pages stay backed by frames. It also removes the recorded grant-holder field and the charge_over function.
> If OD5 stays as written, the docs commit must amend I5, and the model's I5 check must allow it.
> 
> P2-3 Runs are never reclaimed during a process's life. unmap keeps the frame and the run, and the table has 32 runs per device, so a driver that allocates and unmaps dynamically gets OutOfMemory for the rest of its life. It is also charged for every page it ever allocated. Confirm with blkd and D3's netd that each allocates a bounded pool at start (in runs and pages). State in the dma_alloc row that DMA memory is held until the process ends.
> 
> P2-4 The attack case must not pass vacuously, and the must-fail run must fail for the stated reason.
> - Require the reuse to be proven (the same physical address, via the test's own dma_alloc). No reuse is an inconclusive FAIL on both sides, not a pass.
> - The pre-K5b run must record observed DMA into the attacker-steered address, not just a failed expect line.
> - dma-reset-quarantine's 'frames never come back' needs a real search: allocate until the pool (or a bounded large count) is exhausted and assert no quarantined phys appears.
> - Add the co-holder sub-case from P1-1.
> 
> P2-5 Non-virtio DMA devices always quarantine. reset() returns false, so every death of a process whose S contains a non-virtio DMA device quarantines all of its runs and flags that device until reboot, even when the device never saw those frames (OD3 puts every map_device'd DMA device in S). Say so as a platform residual (FPGA and other non-virtio DMA get no restart). Consider flagging only devices that actually held runs, or that were mapped while the process held runs.
> 
> P3:
> 1. Clear the OD3 mapped-device bitmask and every run's holder at terminate. dma_release must consider only Live runs, so that a reused PID never re-processes old Quarantined runs.
> 2. Quarantine doesn't unmap the flagged device from live co-holders (Q144: mappings outlive handles). State it as the residual beside OD3's.
> 3. Billing: under K5's approved rule (s7), destroy work is billed to the dying budget and syscall work to the caller. Bill the reset poll the same way, not 'whichever budget is current'.
> 4. Fix the rv64 window address in the plan and add a boot assert against PLIC, physmap and other kernel windows (rv32 already has one). Confirm the root entry is shared into every process's root.
> 5. The boot classification read of magic and version is harmless for virtio, but other DMA devices in Devs can have read-to-clear registers. Restrict the read to devices the platform marks virtio-mmio, or state it.
> 6. The worst case for K5's latency table: |S| x 1 ms, non-preemptible, on top of R10's ~21 ms. Add it to the sched-latency notes.

### K5 red team · Reply

Event: `c6923666d6393d1094f69395ea1fdc80` · 2026-09-24T21:13:17Z

> K5b plan v2 red-team re-review. Read-only; I read the whole plan once, and the constants at ce95d19ba.
> 
> VERDICT: OK with notes. P1-1 and all the P2s are closed. There is one new P2 (the order of the charge migration, a one-line change) and three P3s. None needs another plan round; fold them in during implementation.
> 
> P1-1 CLOSED.
> - reset() returns false without touching a quarantined or non-virtio slot, so such a slot is never in confirmed_now.
> - Step 3 pools only when S is a subset of confirmed_now, and both asserts are per-release. The weak epoch comparison is gone.
> - Step 4 quarantines every Live run of the dying pid, runs through healthy slots included, and re-flagging an already-flagged slot is idempotent.
> - 'deaf fails only the first attempt' makes the D1/D2 sub-case decisive. A buggy skip-as-confirmed, or a retry, would let D2's second reset confirm and pool, and the exhaustive search plus D2's budget_usage would catch it.
> - K5bQuarantinedSlotCountsAsReset and the model's FirstFails device plus the co-holder generator mirror it.
> 
> P2-1 CLOSED as ruled (DMA slots only; the log-server's UART grant at 0x10000000 overlaps no virtio slot, which start at 0x10001000). P3-a below covers the overlap arithmetic.
> P2-2 CLOSED in intent (the charge stays on run.charged; I5 holds), but see N1 on ordering.
> P2-3 CLOSED: the ABI row, blkd 1 run (kernel.rs:67, allocated once), netd 2 runs before thread_create.
> P2-4 CLOSED: reuse proven by phys through dma_alloc, with inconclusive FAIL forbidden; the must-fail run requires observed steered DMA; exhaustive search (but see P3-c).
> P2-5 CLOSED as a stated platform residual, and the reason not to narrow it (a mapped device can hold any of the process's frame addresses) is right.
> P3s CLOSED:
> - the rv64 window at 0xffff_ffff_f400_0000 = KERNEL_PLIC_BASE (0xffff_ffff_f000_0000) + 64 MiB, under the shared root 511, clear of the stacks (fff8_0000) and the image;
> - rv32 at 0xff7f_0000, below PROCESS_AREA 0xff80_0000, with the PLIC-end assert;
> - the boot read limited to loader DMA-flagged (virtio-compatible) entries, with the residual;
> - billing per K5's rule; Live-only runs and state cleared at terminate; the co-holder mapping residual.
> Consistency: OD1-OD7, s2 and the tests agree, with no superseded text.
> 
> N1 (P2) Migrate quarantine charges after return_carve, not before.
> s3 says 'before return_carve(top), every quarantined run charged to a dying budget is re-charged to top's parent, with a plain charge that cannot fail (argued in OD5 and asserted)'. OD5's argument, however, rests on the parent getting back the child's whole carve, which happens in return_carve. Before it, the parent's usage still includes the child's carve, so a limit-checked charge (budget.rs charge() returns Result and boot code .expect()s it) can fail for a parent near its limit, and the assert would panic the kernel (I14).
> Fix: run return_carve(top) first, then charge the parent (q <= top's limit <= the carve just returned, as argued), or apply both as one net adjustment. Keep the assert. Mirror the same order in the model's destroy_budget, and let I5 be checked after each step.
> 
> P3:
> (a) Define 'overlaps a DMA registry slot' by page-rounded ranges. Refuse if [floor(phys), ceil(phys + size)) intersects [floor(base), ceil(base + len)) of any slot, using the Devs entry's length, not only the base. On platforms that pack several device windows into one page, a non-DMA grant on a page shared with a DMA device must be refused too (or the loader must reject such a grant). Test a partial-page and an adjacent-page mapping in dma-rules.
> (b) DMA devices beyond MAX_DMA_DEVICES lose the flag but stay physically DMA-capable. After that they are not in any S, and legacy MapMemory isn't refused for them. Fail closed harder: create no device object for them (the kernel can't police them), and include them in the legacy refusal. Irrelevant on QEMU virt (8 slots); relevant for ports.
> (c) The exhaustive search allocates only against system and one child of users. Any other budget with free pages (the test's own leftover budgets, D1/D2's parents after migration) leaves pool frames the checker never draws, and a wrongly pooled quarantined frame could sit among them. Either destroy every other non-boot budget before searching, or allocate against every budget that still has free pages, and assert the checker's total equals the free-frame count, e.g. from budget_usage(root).
